content:
## Request Context
- **What was requested**: Unify /distribute and /onboard into ONE command that, pointed at any project path, UPDATES the framework if present or APPLIES it if absent — both routes producing an up-front human-readable value/risk report (features added, what changes, conflicts & losses framed as 'deploy this and you lose X', plus backflow/blast-radius). Deploy gated on a clean tree, lands on a dedicated back-out-able branch, never push/auto-merge, one target at a time.
- **Files/scope**: SPEC-20260524-203931; reuses ef9a485 (change_package.py, assessment.py, stage_branch.py, repo_safety_check.py) + /onboard's takeover steps; new = router, greenfield classifier mode, feature/change interpretation, report assembler.
- **Developer-stated motivation**: One mental model for 'apply or update the framework on this project, show value/risk first, then deploy safely'; today it's two commands split at lineage-presence and the dry-run only emits counts. Core fear: clobbering authored work in a downstream project.
- **Explicit constraints**: Preserve the B1 mechanical floor on BOTH routes (never silently overwrite authored work); assess strictly read-only (works on dirty repos); deploy clean-tree-gated; never push/auto-merge; reuse don't rebuild; the greenfield consent asymmetry (human-adopts-own-project vs derived-project opt-in hard gate) is a Prime-Objective call requiring a Steward gate before build.

VERDICT approve-with-changes (0.82). F1 (medium): greenfield classification should be a SIBLING mode, not an overload of compute_package/_classify (which is bound to drift_scan/pinned/accept-deny); extract the floor decision as a shared primitive + a thin compute_greenfield_package, both returning ChangePackage so the report assembler and stage stay baseline-agnostic — keeps the B1 floor in ONE auditable place. F2 (medium): the report assembler serves two phases with different shapes; factor shared section-builders (scrubbed-diff, consent-stakes order, counted disclaimer, backflow) and compose TWO assemblers (existing staging build_assessment_doc + new build_assess_report with the Features-added section); do NOT duplicate redact_secrets/disclaimer. F3: write a SUCCESSOR ADR (supersede ADR-0017), not an amendment — the unified model changes ADR-0017 central consent premise. F4: do NOT hard-code the greenfield consent answer ahead of the Steward gate; keep the consent check a pluggable deploy preflight. F5 (endorse): R5 light-apply + handoff is the right boundary; do not inline the heavy takeover. F6: prefer /onboard survives as a thin alias to the deeper takeover, not full retirement; /apply-framework is the clearest name.

VERDICT 2 BLOCKING + 4 advisory (0.87). BLOCKING F1 (A03 prompt injection): greenfield feeds arbitrary target file content into the R6 agent interpretation; spec must EXPLICITLY extend the B1 R3a data-only framing (wrap target content as data-not-instructions) to the APPLY route + add an AC; the escalate-only gate blocks demotion but the free-text anchoring path stays open. BLOCKING F2 (A01 / testable consent): the Steward-ratified greenfield consent model must feed back into a CONCRETE testable AC and specify which gating function APPLY calls instead of the opt-in check (repo_safety_check today blocks on missing manifest); a builder reading the spec now could ship APPLY with only a clean-tree check. ADVISORY F3: baseline_gate_green executes the target own quality_gate.py (code-exec) — on an untrusted greenfield target, skip or warn before running. F4: mandate redact_secrets on the NEW greenfield report path via an AC (target CLAUDE.md / .claude/settings.json may carry secrets). F5: symlink containment on the READ path (assessment _read_text / change_package target reads) — low, single-owner. F6: the pre-deploy assess report must be ephemeral / counts-only in hub capture (confidentiality, ADR-0017 R7). Strengths: escalate-only reclassify, redact_secrets fail-closed, _validate_ref_name + _resolve_within, list-form subprocess, never-push.

VERDICT 5 blocking test-seam gaps + 3 advisory (0.87). KEYSTONE QUESTION: resolve whether the greenfield classifier REUSES _classify with an empty drift_map (then it inherits the existing floor + TestNoneDriftClassification/stale_baseline regression for the drift-None arm) vs a NEW code path (then a new regression is owed). BLOCKING: (1) add a regression-ledger entry + a regression-tagged test test_greenfield_existing_file_is_value_unverified_not_silent (B1 extends to greenfield = same Abstraction-Narrowing class); (2) define a greenfield_env fixture (target with NO lineage YAML, NO DB, own CLAUDE.md + .claude/agents/existing.md at framework paths, lacking others) — all 4 existing fixtures are UPDATE-route; (3) specify the assess-never-mutates protocol: snapshot git status --porcelain on a DIRTY target, run assess, assert identical (not just no-exception); (4) deploy clean-gate test: assess-on-dirty succeeds, deploy-on-dirty fails with a message containing dirty/uncommitted; (5) back-out test: capture main SHA, deploy, delete branch, assert main unchanged + staged files absent. ADVISORY: four-section report-structure test (route each classification to the right section incl you-would-lose language); a CLAUDE.md-specific greenfield assertion; route-detection edge cases (lineage absent but .claude present; malformed lineage fails-closed not silently-applies; missing target path). Split AC#7 into pre-Steward (update opt-in test) + post-Steward (apply consent test). Strengths: R6 deterministic boundary (test assembly not prose) is mature; existing UPDATE corpus strong.

VERDICT REVISE before Steward gate (0.82). BLOCKING-1 (Prime Objective consent): R8 uses lineage-ABSENCE as the consent-model selector, which is orthogonal to and inversely correlated with ownership — the least-protected route (APPLY) is the easiest to point at a repo you do NOT own (a fork, a client repo, a colleague checkout), exactly the third-party-benefit-without-consent the Prime Objective forbids (ADR-0015 test b). Require an EXPLICIT captured ownership/authority affirmation on APPLY; best (Alternative 3): write an accepts_distribution-class assent artifact INTO the target as deploy step zero so both routes converge on one human-authored assent record. Present to the Steward as an OPEN CHOICE, not a ratification (the spec recommended-default framing pre-loads it). BLOCKING-2 (mechanical claim vs reality): preserve-the-B1-floor-on-both-routes + reuse-repo_safety_check cannot be honored as written — the floor depends on drift_scan (manifest+DB, absent greenfield) and repo_safety_check FUSES manifest-presence+opt-in+clean-tree into one verdict that blocks EVERY greenfield target; need (a) the greenfield floor as a new impl, ideally an injected Baseline protocol (LineageBaseline + OnDiskBaseline) feeding ONE floor tested against both, and (b) a SEPARABLE clean-tree-only check. ADVISORY: report route as a SPECTRUM (no lineage but N pre-existing framework-path files), not binary; BOUND the greenfield offer set + tier R6 per-category not per-file (else unbounded cost + banner-blindness); put single-report-front-end + two-route-engines-behind-it (Alternative 2) to the Steward as the leading candidate vs full code-path unification (delivers one-command UX while preserving consent + knowledge-state boundaries + defending route divergence); strip recommended-default framing before the gate. Strengths: assess read-only invariant; R4 policy instinct right (new tests owed).

## Request Context
- What was requested: unify /distribute + /onboard into ONE command that updates the framework if present or applies it if absent on any target path, with an up-front value/risk report; deploy gated on clean tree, dedicated back-out branch, never push/auto-merge, one target at a time.
- Files/scope: SPEC-20260524-203931; reuses ef9a485 distribute scripts + /onboard steps.
- Developer-stated motivation: one mental model; core fear is clobbering authored work downstream.
- Explicit constraints: preserve B1 floor both routes; assess read-only; deploy clean-tree-gated; never push/auto-merge; greenfield consent asymmetry is Steward-gated.

## Synthesis
Net verdict: REVISE before the Steward gate (arch approve-with-changes 0.82; security 2-blocking 0.87; qa 5-blocking-seams 0.87; independent REVISE 0.82). The front-end (route-aware ASSESS read-only -> human reads value/risk -> gated DEPLOY) is sound and worth building. Two convergent BLOCKING themes, plus folded mechanical fixes.

BLOCKING-A (consent / Prime Objective; independent + security): R8 used lineage-ABSENCE as the consent-model selector, which is inversely correlated with ownership — the least-protected route (APPLY) is the easiest to aim at a repo the operator does not own (fork/client/colleague), exactly the third-party-benefit-without-consent the Prime Objective forbids. RESOLUTION (Steward-gated, presented as OPEN not pre-loaded): require an explicit captured ownership/authority affirmation on APPLY; recommended Alternative-3 = write an accepts_distribution-class assent artifact INTO the target as deploy step zero, so both routes converge on one human-authored assent record.

BLOCKING-B (mechanical claim vs reality; independent + arch + qa): preserve-B1-floor-both-routes + reuse-repo_safety_check cannot be honored as written. FOLDED: greenfield floor becomes a new impl behind an injected Baseline protocol (LineageBaseline + OnDiskBaseline) feeding ONE floor primitive, tested against both (kills route divergence); repo_safety_check split into separable manifest-presence / opt-in / clean-tree checks so deploy gates on clean-tree alone.

FOLDED mechanical fixes: extend B1 R3a data-only framing to the greenfield agent interpretation (+AC) [security F1]; two report assemblers sharing section-builders, no duplicated redact_secrets/disclaimer, build_assess_report for the 4-section assess report [arch F2]; SUCCESSOR ADR superseding ADR-0017 not an amendment [arch F3]; greenfield report path must redact_secrets (+AC) [security F4]; baseline_gate_green skip/warn on untrusted greenfield [security F3]; pre-deploy report ephemeral/counts-only in hub capture [security F6]; bound the greenfield offer set + tier R6 per-category [independent]; route reported as a SPECTRUM not binary [independent]; test seams as explicit ACs — greenfield_env fixture, regression-ledger + regression test, assess-immutability via git status --porcelain on a dirty target, deploy clean-gate test, back-out test, four-section report test; split AC#7 pre/post-Steward [qa]; /onboard survives as a thin alias to the deeper takeover, /apply-framework name [arch F6]; symlink read-path containment deferred to v1.1 (single-owner) [security F5].

ELEVATED to developer + Steward (open, not pre-decided): (A) the APPLY consent model above; (B) architecture — independent recommends single-report-front-end + TWO route engines behind it (Alternative 2) over full code-path unification: it delivers the one-command UX the developer asked for while preserving the consent + knowledge-state boundaries and defending against route divergence. Spec revised to status:reviewed; both elevated decisions go to the Steward gate before /build_module.
